title: A 7T MRI Study of Fibular Bone Thickness and Density: Impact of Age, Sex and Body Weight, and Correlation with Bone Marrow Expansion and Muscle Fat Infiltration
content: Reduced bone mass and density, hallmark features of osteopenia and osteoporosis, significantly increase the risk of fractures, falls, and loss of mobility, especially in postmenopausal women and the elderly. This quantitative 7T MRI study examines fibular bone thinning and density decrease in 107 individuals (43F/64M) across various ages, body mass indices (BMI), and ethnicities. Women had significantly lower cross-sectional bone-wall thickness (BT) and bone-tissue area (BA) along with greater bone density decrease compared to men, with significant differences observed only in those over age 50 (n = 77), not in the younger group (n = 30). The bone g-factor, defined as the ratio of inner-to-outer bone diameters, increased with bone thinning, bone marrow expansion (BME), and muscle fat infiltration (MFI), but was independent of subcutaneous fat thickness (SFT). Bone density decrease correlated with bone mass loss, with a stronger association observed with BT than BA. These findings offer insights into the effects of aging and sex on skeletomuscular health, with implications for strategies to mitigate bone loss in osteoporosis and osteosarcopenia.
